title: Use of a new hd-PTFE membrane in alveolar socket preservation (Permamem®): a case series Jean
authors: Michel Heurtebise, Séverine Vincent-Bugnas 2019. Poster EAO Lisbon.
studyType: Poster or congress abstract (not peer reviewed)
supports: NOT PEER REVIEWED — this is a congress poster or abstract, not a journal publication, whatever study type its own title claims. Treat it as the weakest tier of all and never present it as a published study. Clinical study from the botiss permamem (dense PTFE) literature list — the product featured in it, which is not the same as the study being about the product, so check the design and the comparator before citing it as product evidence. Abstract, verbatim (no separate conclusion section): “permamem.pdf#new_tab Following a tooth extraction there is a post-extractional bone resorption. This is why an alveolar socket preservation technique is recommended to limit this pattern and to ensure the bone volume for an eventually implant prosthetic restauration. We want to check if an alveolar socket preservation is possible with no attempt of primary wound closure using a high density PTFE membrane (permamem®) exposed to the oral environment. Five patients aged from 23 to 61 who needed an extraction of a molar were chosen. In all cases a CBCT scanner was done before the extraction. Once the atraumatic extraction was completed, the alveolar socket was filled with a xenogenic bone graft (BioOss ®, Geistlich) and covered with a high density PTFE membrane. There was no attempt of fully coverage of the membrane. Three months later another CBCT scanner was realised.
